title: Arbitration provisions as contract-formation questions
summary: Before enforcing an arbitration clause, a court must determine whether the parties agreed to that clause under the applicable rules of contract formation and term inclusion.
notes:
Specht, Dorton, C. Itoh, Hill, Klocek, and Anderson reach this question through different transaction structures. Some concern whether notice and conduct establish assent; others concern whether an additional term entered an existing contract. Graham separately examines an arbitration arrangement for unfairness even where the provision was expected. Agreement, scope, enforceability, and the particular procedural request are distinct questions.

Specht concerns notice and manifestation; Dorton asks whether arbitration was already agreed or a material added term; C. Itoh excludes it from a conduct-based contract; Hill and Klocek disagree about later terms. These decisions do not decide the underlying claims simply by resolving the forum question. Each opinion’s applicable law and evidentiary posture determine how agreement is assessed.
